output1RuleAndViolationIdentifier.rule: A block is invalid if a transaction committed by its `transactions_root` carries a validity interval the block's own time range does not cover, or a malformed one. The block header states an inclusive `startTime` and an exclusive `endTime`; every transaction it commits must be valid throughout that window, so a normalized transaction range whose lower bound precedes the block's start, whose upper bound reaches the block's end, or that is empty or inverted, is a fault the on-chain family proves in two steps: step-01 binds the challenged transaction under the header's counted transactions root and forwards the block window together with the normalized range, and step-02 finalizes on the fact that the range does not cover the window.

localEnforcement.note: The malformed-interval half of the rule, decided on the transaction alone: a negative bound that is not the unbounded sentinel, and a lower bound above the upper bound. Both sites sit inside `validateValidityInterval`. The identifier token is measured to appear in this file at exactly these two lines and nowhere else, so the count is the enforcement count rather than a count of mentions, and each site's `return reject(` opener is required two lines above the token so a comparison or a log line carrying the same token could not be counted as enforcement.

The uncovered-interval half: the same lower-bound and upper-bound pair of checks against the block's sampled slot, on each of the two candidate-application paths — four sites, two per path. As above, the token is measured to appear in this file at exactly these four lines and nowhere else, and each site's `return fail(` opener is required on the line immediately above the token.

output1RuleAndViolationIdentifier.enforcementNote: The family corrects two local identifiers rather than one, which is what the coverage matrix's own Local cell for this row states, so both are bound here: a malformed interval is decided in phase-a on the transaction alone, and an interval the block window does not cover is decided in phase-b against the sampled slot. The declaration for each identifier is re-derived in the verifier from its recorded key and identifier string and required to be present in demo/midgard-validation/src/types.ts, rather than quoted, so a renamed key or a re-lettered code fails here.

familyStateRecords.note: This family carries only ONE family-owned `Args` record, so the record parity output 2 asks for would be thin if it stopped there. Set equality is the strongest claim measurable from tracked files: the Aiken side of this enum is `aiken_design_patterns/validity_range_normalization`, a third-party package that is fetched into onchain/aiken/build/packages rather than committed here, so its positional constructor order cannot be read from this tree without depending on a populated build cache. output3FlatFieldHashBinding.bindingNote: This family opens NONE of the nine committed fields, and that is a measured fact rather than an omission: the whole section-2.5 inventory is parsed out of the spec's own table by the verifier and no commitment slot in it names the validity interval. What binds them is therefore the section-3 transaction identity: step-01 re-derives the challenged transaction's id from the compact bytes it carries and verifies that id under the header's counted `transactions_root`, and the two scalars are read out of that same authenticated structure. There is no preimage to carry, no field-hash to authenticate a second time, and no field-opening argument in either step's redeemer. That is why the section-8 field-preimage carriage tiers and the spend-input cardinality axis do not reach this family, and why its steps cannot exhibit the abort-never-clamp exposure of section 7 item 3 at a collection offset: the read is by record field, not by index into a committed collection. The section-7 access invariants are still anchored because the abort-never-clamp discipline is what makes the unbounded sentinel a decision rather than a clamped bound: the family's normalizer maps `-1` on either side to an explicitly unbounded arm of the normalized range and maps an inverted pair to `InvalidRange`, instead of silently repairing either.

output4OnchainSelectors.claim: Every deployed step of the family carries at least one step-scoped positive selector and at least one valid-block negative selector, and all of them are measured passing in one batched run under the pinned fork compiler.
output4OnchainSelectors.selectionNote: `aiken check -m <module>.{<test>}` names exactly one test, so the batch is exact: the run must collect precisely the declared selectors and no others. `aiken check` exits 0 on a selector that matches nothing, so a zero-collection or partial-collection run has to be failed by the derivation rather than by the exit code. The declared set is additionally cross-checked against every `test` declaration the two modules contain, so a selector added to one of these modules and left uncited fails this gate.
output4OnchainSelectors.scopeNote: Each selector carries a `scope` beside its role, and the distinction is load-bearing rather than decorative. Three of step-01's ten selectors are unit cases of the module-local `normalize_native_validity_range` helper: they exercise the one-tick interval, the empty interval and the unbounded sentinel directly, without going through the `main.spend` handler. They are real guards and they are counted, but a per-module `positives > 0` check would have been satisfied by those three ALONE — so this family's output 4 could have been published met with both of step-01's real proof-step positives deleted. The requirement is therefore stated on step-scoped positives: every module must carry at least one positive that drives its own `main.spend` handler, and both counts are published so a reader of the summary cannot mistake one for the other.

selectors.claim: The normalizer's inclusive-lower/exclusive-upper contract at its tightest: a one-tick interval survives normalization as a closed range of a single point rather than collapsing to empty.
An interval whose exclusive upper bound is not above its lower bound normalizes to `InvalidRange` — the arm step-02 finalizes on unconditionally — instead of being repaired into a valid range.

The `-1` sentinel of body positions 4 and 5 becomes an explicitly unbounded arm of the normalized range rather than a numeric bound of minus one, which is the abort-never-clamp discipline of spec section 7 at this family's own read.

The step-scoped positive: the challenged transaction is genuinely committed under the block's counted `transactions_root`, so its re-derived id binds and the block window together with the normalized validity range of the challenged transaction reaches step-02 through the real `main.spend` handler on a genuine native-V1 block fixture.

The same binding through a deep membership proof carried by published chunks — the carriage route added at issue #545, past the direct route's envelope ceiling — with the block window and normalized range still reaching step-02.
Published chunks stay bound to the header's counted transactions root; a forged root cannot bind.
The step is bound to the exact claim its redeemer named, so a merkelized verifier invoked on a different chunk order proves nothing this step asked for.

A transaction fabricated against a VALID block's header cannot bind: the raw transactions root is not the one that header's counted `transactions_root` commits, so the challenge dies before any interval claim is forwarded.

The terminal decision over every uncovered shape the normalized range can take: a closed range that starts before the block window or reaches its exclusive end, a lower-unbounded range that reaches the end, an upper-unbounded range that starts before the beginning, and the inverted `InvalidRange` arm. The `Always` arm is the one shape that is not a fault and is failed explicitly rather than accepted.
A transaction whose normalized range is covered by the block window cannot be finalized as a fault: the terminal step refuses the challenge instead of minting a proof token against a valid block.

delegatedOutputs.rationale: Outputs 5 to 8 are not unowned and are not re-derived here. They are bound family-locally for Q12 inside the SHARED four-family artifact, whose own gate is the executable authority for those cells and runs in the same battery as this one. That gate spawns five Vitest suites, including three emulator suites that drive the complete correction path at forced branch level 22 and at the admissible 296-input Cardano spend shape. Re-running them from this gate would double the battery's cost and would measure nothing the shared gate does not already measure. So this gate delegates the passage and asserts the delegation instead: it re-reads the shared artifact's Q12 cells for outputs 5 to 9, requires each to be LOCAL_PASS with no open cell left anywhere in that artifact, requires the carriage membership that applies to this family and the ABSENCE of the one that does not, and then re-checks in this tree that the concrete Q12 surfaces those cells describe still exist and are still wired.

assertedCells.carriageDispositionNote: This is the one place where this family's delegation contract deliberately differs from its Q10 and Q11 siblings', and copying theirs would have produced a gate that is wrong in one direction or the other. The shared artifact records TWO carriage remediations. `chunkedProofCarriage` (issue #545, remediating finding Q1X-F5) has measured this family: `chunkedProofCarriage.measuredFamilies` is [Q10, Q11, Q12, Q14], and the depth axis is precisely the one that binds here, since this family's step-01 is the tightest of the four and is where the shared artifact's own two-depth marginal measurement is taken. `spendInputTierRoutedCarriage` (issue #612, remediating Q1X-F6) has NOT: its `measuredFamilies` is [Q10, Q11] and its `bindingStages` names step-04 for Q10 and step-02 for Q11 and no stage at all for this family. That is not a gap in the remediation — it is the scope of the axis. The axis's own record, `spendInputCardinalityBound.affectsGoalIds`, is measured to be exactly [Q10, Q11], and the source agrees: neither of this family's steps opens a spend-inputs collection. Step-01's args are the shared inclusion carriage, step-02's are three indices, neither lib module mentions a field opening, and the only `spend_inputs` occurrence anywhere in either validator is the `spend_inputs_hash: ""` slot of a compact-body literal in a unit fixture — a hash field of the committed structure, not an opening of the collection behind it. So this gate requires membership in the chunked remediation, requires ABSENCE from the tier-routed one, and derives which of the two it demands from the axis's own scope list rather than hard-coding either: `spendInputAxisApplies` is required to equal whether this goal id appears in `spendInputCardinalityBound.affectsGoalIds`, and membership in `spendInputTierRoutedCarriage.measuredFamilies` is required to agree with that derivation in BOTH directions. A gate that demanded this family in the tier-routed list would be red forever; a gate that silently skipped the axis would hide a real obligation if the axis ever grew to cover this family. This one fails closed either way and says which way.

Output 9 is nevertheless re-measured locally below by running the emulator suite directly, so this artifact's output-9 row rests on a runner report of its own rather than on a citation.

outputStatus.evidence: The rule is stated as the covering relation it is — the block header's inclusive start and exclusive end against the challenged transaction's normalized range — and this family carries TWO local identifiers, both bound as declarations rather than prose. `InvalidValidityIntervalFormat: "E_INVALID_VALIDITY_INTERVAL_FORMAT"` is enforced at 2 measured `return reject(...)` sites in demo/midgard-validation/src/phase-a.ts (lines 268 and 281, both inside `validateValidityInterval`, for a negative non-sentinel bound and for an inverted pair), and `ValidityIntervalMismatch: "E_VALIDITY_INTERVAL_MISMATCH"` at 4 measured `return fail(...)` sites in demo/midgard-validation/src/phase-b.ts (lines 915, 925, 1097 and 1106 — the lower-bound and upper-bound checks against the sampled slot on each of the two candidate-application paths), 6 sites in total. Each identifier's token is measured to appear in its file at exactly those lines and nowhere else, and each site's rejection opener is required within the enclosing call, so the number is an enforcement count rather than a count of mentions. The deployed identifier side is the catalogue: `invalidRange` is measured at index 3 of FRAUD_PROOF_CATALOGUE_CATEGORY_ORDER among 11 categories, and the append-only 4-byte id 00000003 is re-derived from that index rather than read from a constant. The registered-families lifecycle suite is measured to carry no invalid-range lifecycle and is therefore explicitly not cited; catalogue reachability is carried by the output-9 journey, which asserts both the returned category name and the thread asset name against the deployed `invalidRange` category id.

outputStatus.title: Canonical evidence schema and strict TypeScript/Aiken codec agreement
outputStatus.evidence: Three records are parsed out of both sides and measured field-for-field identical in the same positional order, plus the enum one of them carries.
